tasks.title: Distinguisher candidate generation and the projection-multiplicity ladder, including the gate-RR78 null

handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Which of the generated distinguisher candidates survive their own cheapest falsification control, and whether the projection-multiplicity ladder isolates a property of AES or of round structure generally.

The ladder is run with a COMPONENT NULL (random bijective S-box). If the reading holds for any bijective S-box it is recorded as a fact about round structure, not about AES.
The gate-RR78 evaluation states the algebraic compatibility of the final-round convention with the output space it tests; an incompatible pairing is recorded as a void gate, not as a negative result.
Scaled-down (MINI-AES) readings are identified as analogues and no transfer to GF(2^8) AES is asserted without an argument.
Each surviving candidate states its measured death round and its false-positive rate against the matched control, or states that these were not measured.

tasks.notes: The GATE-RR78-1 null was overturned inside this package: it paired a final round DROPPING MixColumns with an output space valid only when it KEEPS it, so the condition never pulled back through SubBytes.
